conflict_topics: shared cookware cleanliness/who washes shared items
dialogue_quality_notes: Conversation moves from complaint to concrete proposals (scheduling and a house-rule), which is natural and productive. (e.g., Turn 3–4 scheduling exchange; Turn 14 rule proposal).
Few repetitions; turns are concise and on-topic. One participant (A) initially denies responsibility then accepts a rule (Turn 10, Turn 18).
No role confusion; factual claims are limited and consistent with the setting.
evaluation.final_reason: Agent C proposed a household norm: '...can we just agree that if you use a shared pot, you wash it as soon as you're done?' (Turn 14). Agent D accepted: 'Yeah, that's fair.' (Turn 15). Agent A then agreed: 'Fine. As long as we don't just assume who made the mess.' (Turn 18). Thus the shared-pan/cleaning conflict was settled by group acceptance of a 'wash after use' rule, with A adding a condition against presumptive blame. The ventilation/smell request (open window) was not agreed and remains unsettled.
position_change_notes: Agent D: began by stating a scheduling constraint (Turn 1) and later accepted the scheduling compromise implicitly (Turn 3) and supported the cleaning rule (Turn 15).
Agent A: initially defensive about the unwashed pan ('That wasn't me.' Turn 10) but agreed to the 'wash after use' norm in Round 8 ('Fine. ...') and also agreed to finish cooking by 8:15 (Turn 4).
Agent C: consistently pushed for cleaning and proposed the explicit rule (Turn 14); maintained position until others accepted.
Agent B: raised the smell/ventilation problem and requested window opening (Turns 5,7) but did not receive an explicit agreement on that request by the transcript end.

round_scores.evidence: Agent D: 'By the time I can get to the stove, it's already too late for me to start cooking.' Agent A: 'What time do you want to cook?' — a scheduling incompatibility is introduced but not yet resolved.
Agent D: 'I'm usually ready to cook around 8:15.' Agent A: 'Okay, I can be done by 8:15.' — parties agree on a cooking time, resolving the scheduling tension.
Agent B: 'When you cook, can you use the fan and open the window?' Agent A: 'I do use the fan.' — a new smell/ventilation complaint appears and remains unsettled (open window not agreed).

Agent B: 'It's not enough, the smell is all the way to my room. Can you open the window as well?' Agent C: 'Okay, but what about the pan from last night?' — the ventilation complaint intensifies and a separate cleanliness conflict (unwashed pan) is introduced; both unresolved.
Agent A: 'That wasn't me.' Agent C: 'Okay. But it's been here since last night. It needs to be washed.' — continued dispute about who used/should clean the shared pan; no settlement.

Agent A: 'Then whoever used it should wash it.' Agent C: '...Can we just agree that if you use a shared pot, you wash it as soon as you're done?' — a proposed house rule reduces immediate tension but is not yet accepted by all.

Agent D: 'Yeah, that's fair.' Agent C: 'So are we all doing that? Wash it straight after you use it?' — emergence of agreement from D; some outstanding acceptance remains (not everyone has explicitly confirmed).

Agent A: 'Fine. As long as we don't just assume who made the mess.' Agent C: 'Okay. It's not about blaming. Agent B, are you okay with that?' — A explicitly accepts the washing-after-use rule (with a condition); the cleaning issue is effectively settled among those who spoke, but the ventilation/smell request (open window) was not agreed and remains a minor unresolved issue.

substantive_insights: Scheduling conflicts can be resolved quickly by specifying and matching times (Agent D gave 8:15; Agent A agreed).
Cleanliness problems were persistent until a concrete behavioral rule ('wash after use') was proposed and accepted; explicit rules help prevent recurring shared-resource disputes.

Ventilation/odor concerns remained unresolved because the requested mitigation (open window) was not explicitly agreed to, showing that multiple distinct friction points can coexist and require separate agreements.

normalizations: Removed resolution_round 8 because the final status is partially_resolved.
